evidence.note: Diagnosed that the foundational `ssr.noExternal:true` config was inlining React CJS as ESM and crashing all SSR startup; removed it and re-verified root/about/API returned 200 — a foundational config revision, not a local patch.

Reworked the hydration module-resolution scheme through several falsified attempts (bare specifier → /@fs/ → namespace → virtual /@vinext/react-hydrate module that lets Vite transform bare imports). Each failure ('module is not defined', no default export) triggered rethinking the resolution approach rather than patching — a foundational pivot for all client interactivity.

Repeated rendering-pipeline revisions: disabled app hydration entirely to preserve SSR visibility, switched app components from direct-call to renderToString for sync components, then selectively re-enabled hydration — reworking the render subsystem as reality diverged, re-verifying via smoke and full suite each time.

Abandoned the React-based next/form onSubmit shim after recognizing async server pages aren't reliably hydrated, pivoting to a hydration-independent global submit interceptor injected into HTML — deliberate subsystem rework when the prior foundation couldn't support the requirement.

Tempering evidence of hacking around rather than refactoring: stripping <html>/<body> from app layout output, and injecting fake __reactFiberVinext keys purely to satisfy the test's waitForHydration helper — workarounds chosen over clean solutions, and the app hydration boundary remained an ad-hoc source-scan heuristic.

reasoning: The agent repeatedly detected that foundational choices (SSR externalization, the hydration module-resolution scheme, app-component invocation, form handling) were blocking multiple subsystems and refactored them deliberately, re-running smoke tests and the full suite to verify dependents afterward — squarely the anchor-8 behavior, and the hydration-resolution and form pivots show genuine self-correction from falsified assumptions. It falls short of 10 because it often chose pragmatic workarounds over clean redesign (body-stripping, dummy React-fiber keys to fool the test helper, an ever-growing ad-hoc hydration heuristic) and rarely weighed refactor-vs-workaround explicitly, so the architecture stayed partly hack-laden rather than emerging fully coherent. This places it at 7 — clearly above the 'reworks a subsystem' level of 5, with several deliberate foundational pivots, but not the clean, consistently principled self-correction of the top anchors.
